title: Data Analysis Expressions (DAX) - Simply Explained

entities.name: DAX
entities.quote: What exactly is DAX? Is it just Excel formulas inside Power BI or is it something completely different?

entities.name: Semantic model
entities.quote: Power BI gives you the structure, the floors, walls, and rooms. That's your data model.

entities.name: Power BI
entities.quote: Today's topic is one that almost everyone working with Power BI has heard of

entities.name: Microsoft Excel
entities.quote: Is it just Excel formulas inside Power BI or is it something completely different?

quotes.text: Here's the thing, most people think DAX is basically Excel formulas with a different name, but it isn't. DAX is a whole different way of thinking about calculations.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Corrects the most common misconception about DAX.

quotes.text: If the number needs to change when someone clicks a button, use a measure. If it is the same no matter what, a calculated column is fine.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a simple rule for choosing between measures and calculated columns.

quotes.text: Every number you see in a Power BI report is calculated inside something called filter context. It sounds complicated, but it is simple. Filter context is just the set of filters active at that exact moment.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Demystifies filter context in plain language.

quotes.text: Calculate works by temporarily changing the filter context. You give it an expression to calculate and then you give it one or more filters to apply.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains how the most important DAX function works.

quotes.text: The real power of DAX isn't about memorizing 100 functions. It's about clean data modeling and a few core patterns. Get the model right and the DAX becomes almost obvious.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the episode's main lesson about modeling over memorization.

takeaways: DAX works on whole tables and columns rather than cells, so treating it like Excel formulas leads to wrong results.
Prefer measures over calculated columns, because measures recalculate in the current filter context while columns stay static and bloat the model.
Master filter context and CALCULATE, use iterators only for row-by-row logic, and mark a proper date table so time intelligence works.
hook: Many Power BI users think DAX is just Excel formulas with a new name and then wonder why their numbers don't add up. This episode explains DAX in plain English for Power BI beginners and analysts: measures versus calculated columns, filter context, CALCULATE, iterators, time intelligence and the pitfalls to avoid.
